minutes.headline: School Committee tabled its FY20 budget vote and sent the superintendent back to the town manager for more money
minutes.summary: The superintendent presented the recommended budget at the town manager's target increase, with named cuts to close the gap from the December proposal. Residents urged the committee to back the higher December budget or pursue an override. The committee tabled the budget vote, then handled line-item transfers, minutes, policies, a food truck pilot, summer extended day dates and the Fund Our Future resolution before going into executive session.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to table the FY20 budget and charged the superintendent to meet her leadership team and request a meeting with the town manager.
The recommended budget was presented at the town manager's target increase, with supply, book, equipment and health insurance trims and several staff positions cut to close the gap.
Residents urged the committee to back the higher December budget or pursue an override; one asked what there is to lose by not seeking one.
The committee tabled the Fund Our Future resolution to its workshop agenda and approved three line-item transfers as presented.
The committee approved a food truck pilot, summer extended day dates, and a rule letting relocating grade 10-12 students stay at Lunenburg High through graduation.

why_it_matters: The school budget for next year is still unsettled, and the outcome of talks with the town manager decides whether the cuts to staff and programs stand or whether residents are asked to vote on an override.
Staff positions, including a greenhouse manager, a language teacher and paraprofessional hours, were named as cuts, so classroom and program levels depend on how the gap is closed.
